scope: Round 9. Homepage change from SRS.txt ('system - Ui change'): the homepage shows trending auctions only, for both guests and logged-in users, plus a 'Just completed' section of exactly 8 closed auctions returned by the API. The UI follows the 1a Browse section of 'Auction Mockups.dc.html' (now in the repo root). Builds on round 8 (archived as progress-feature-list/feature_list_8.json): the card, chip bar, sort control and top bar from ui-1a.1-3 stay. Every business rule from rounds 1-8 stays: bids are checked against available credit and the increment ladder, all deletes are soft (deleted_at), cancelled lots are never listed.

source_requirements.text: Modify homepage to show trending auction only, both logged and un-logged users; just completed auction show 8 closed auction

source_design.file: Auction Mockups.dc.html (repo root, untracked), section 1a 'Browse - auction cards'
source_design.homepage: Top bar; category chip bar; heading 'Trending lots' with subtitle '<n> live auctions · bids update in real time'; 'Sort: Most bids' and 'Price' controls on the right; 4-column grid of lot cards (56px thumb + title + time pill + category pill, 'Highest bid' + bid count, your-bid strip Leading / Outbid / You haven't bid yet, 'Bid $X' and 'Custom bid' buttons). The mockup has no 'Starting soon' section and no 'Just completed' section; the completed section reuses the same card in its ended state.

readings_to_confirm: 'Trending' = live lots (started, not ended, not cancelled, not deleted), ordered by most bids, ties broken by soonest ending. This replaces round 8's decision that the default order stays 'soonest ending'.
'Show trending auction only' = the 'Starting soon' (upcoming) section leaves the homepage. Upcoming lots are still reachable by direct link, My auctions and staff pages, but not from homepage search.

'8 closed auctions' = the 8 most recently closed lots (status ended, or end time passed before the close job ran), newest end time first, with no 7-day window. Fewer than 8 are shown only when fewer than 8 exist (or match the filters).
Search, category chip and 'Ending soon' chip filter both sections, as today. The sort control orders only the trending section; 'Just completed' always stays newest first.

The user's uncommitted card restyle (fe/src/components/AuctionCard.tsx, AuctionBits.tsx, TopSearch.tsx, styles.css, e2e/ui-1a-3-quick-bid.spec.ts) is treated as the baseline and built on, not reverted. Ask the user to commit it, or confirm it may go into home-1.2's commit, before starting.

conventions.tests: Playwright e2e specs go in e2e/ as <id>-<slug>.spec.ts (id with the dot replaced by a dash, e.g. e2e/home-1-2-trending-section.spec.ts). API/integration tests use vitest in be/tests/ as <area>.<topic>.test.ts; frontend unit tests sit next to the code (fe/src/**/*.test.ts). fe vitest has no DOM: keep logic (section split, ordering, labels) in plain modules and cover the React wiring in e2e.
conventions.existing_tests: Keep the existing data-testids on the equivalent element: the trending section keeps data-testid='section-live' and the completed section keeps 'section-completed'; live-count, sort, category-chips, auction-card-<id>, countdown, my-bid-strip, quick-bid, custom-bid stay. When a feature changes visible text or structure an older spec checks (guest-002, guest-003, ui-1a-1, ui-1a-2, ui-1a-3, be/tests/homepage.test.ts, be/tests/auctions.filter-sort.test.ts), update the spec to check the new behaviour. Do not delete or weaken it.
conventions.change_docs: Each feature writes docs/changes/<id>.md listing the files it added or changed and why. home-1.2 / home-2.2 add a 'Homepage' entry to docs/design-system.md.
conventions.responsive: The mockup is drawn at 1440px. The homepage must also work at 375px with no horizontal page scroll: the grid collapses to one column. Each UI e2e spec checks 375px.
conventions.accessibility: Sections use <section aria-labelledby> with an <h2>. Pills carry text, not colour alone. Contrast meets WCAG AA.
conventions.no_fake_data: Mockup values with no source ('1,284 live auctions' as a fixed number, 'bids update in real time' if cards do not update live) are not built as static text.
conventions.soft_delete: All deletes are soft: lots with deleted_at set never appear in either section.
conventions.run_all: ./init.sh (npm install + npm run verify = vitest + fe build + Playwright) must exit 0 before a feature moves to passing. Stop running Docker containers / dev servers first (CLAUDE.md), otherwise prisma generate hits EPERM. Playwright runs with workers: 1, so a spec that creates 9 ended lots can rely on them being the newest.

status_legend.in_progress: The feature is the current active task.
status_legend.blocked: Work cannot continue until a documented blocker is resolved.
status_legend.passing: Required verification has passed and evidence is recorded.

roles.guest: Not signed in. Sees the same homepage sections as a customer, without the your-bid strip.
roles.customer: A signed-in user. Sees the same sections plus their own bid position on each trending card.

features.title: Auctions API: just-completed list returns the 8 most recently closed lots
features.user_visible_behavior: GET /api/auctions returns at most 8 closed lots in its completed part, newest end time first, whatever their age. The response says how many it returns (justCompletedLimit: 8) instead of a day window.
acceptance: Closed = status 'ended', or end time passed before the close job ran; status 'cancelled' and deleted_at set are excluded.
take: 8, ordered by endTime desc, then id desc. The 7-day JUST_COMPLETED_DAYS window is removed.
With 10 closed lots the API returns exactly the 8 newest; with 3 it returns 3.
The sort param does not reorder the completed lots (newest first always).
q/field and category filter the completed lots before the limit (8 newest matches). endingSoon=1 returns no completed lots, as today.
Response field justCompletedDays replaced by justCompletedLimit: 8; fe/src/pages/Home.tsx and the Auction list type updated in the same change.
Same result for a guest and a logged-in customer.
